response.sql:
WITH execution_stats AS (
  SELECT
    oe.ordersmark,
    AVG(oe.fillcount) as order_avg_fill
  FROM orderexecutions oe
  WHERE oe.ordersmark IS NOT NULL AND oe.fillcount IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY oe.ordersmark
),
timespan_stats AS (
  SELECT
    o.timespan,
    AVG(oe.fillcount) as timespan_avg_fill
  FROM orderexecutions oe
  JOIN orders o ON oe.ordersmark = o.recordvault
  WHERE oe.fillcount IS NOT NULL AND o.timespan IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY o.timespan
),
filtered_orders AS (
  SELECT
    es.ordersmark,
    o.timespan,
    es.order_avg_fill,
    es.order_avg_fill - ts.timespan_avg_fill as above_avg,
    RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY o.timespan ORDER BY es.order_avg_fill DESC NULLS LAST) as rnk
  FROM execution_stats es
  JOIN orders o ON es.ordersmark = o.recordvault
  JOIN timespan_stats ts ON o.timespan = ts.timespan
  WHERE es.order_avg_fill > ts.timespan_avg_fill
)
SELECT
  ordersmark,
  timespan,
  order_avg_fill,
  above_avg,
  rnk as rank
FROM filtered_orders
WHERE rnk <= 3
ORDER BY timespan, rnk

assumptions.assumption: The average fill for a timespan is the average of all individual fillcount values across all executions in that timespan (not the average of order-level averages). This interprets 'time in force's average fill' as the aggregate metric across all orders sharing that timespan.

alternatives.interpretation: The average fill for a timespan is the average of each order's average fill (order-level averages). This would weight each order equally regardless of execution count.
